name: folha-bone
prompt: Character model sheet of ONE original cartoon mascot, drawn six times in a 3 columns x 2 rows grid, each pose centered in its own cell with generous empty space around it, full body visible, same character with identical proportions and outfit in every cell. Style: 1950s American print-advertising mascot, mid-century cartoon, clean vector line art like a professional character designer's ink drawing: smooth confident curves, thick uniform black outlines, a few thinner black interior lines for folds and features. COLOR RULES (strict, needed for vectorizing): pure white background; the entire character (skin, hair, clothes, cap, shoes interiors) filled with ONE flat light gray (#C8C8C8); outlines and details pure black; shoes and pupils solid black; no shading, no gradients, no halftone, no texture, no drop shadows, no ground shadows, no color, no text or labels anywhere except where specified. The character: a cheerful young male operator with a big head (about one third of his height) in three-quarter view facing the viewer's right, rounded chin, simple oval eyes, expressive eyebrows, wide confident grin. He wears a 1950s service-station attendant cap (rounded crown, stiff band, short visor pointing to the viewer's right) with the same small round three-lines emblem on the front; a little short hair visible at the back above the ear. Outfit: a one-piece work jumpsuit with a soft collar, a curved yoke seam across the chest, a small round chest patch with a simple emblem of three lines merging into an arrow, a belt with a rectangular buckle, cuffed sleeves, slightly tapered trouser legs, simple rounded shoes. Arms and legs are full and sturdy with natural cartoon curvature (sleeves taper from shoulder to wrist, elbows bend smoothly), hands are four-finger cartoon hands. Do NOT draw: a thumbs-up, a wink, a vertical stripe down the jumpsuit, any number on the clothing, a blond curl. The six poses: 1) PROUD: one fist on his hip with the elbow pointing out, the other hand raised beside his face making an OK sign (thumb and index finger in a circle, other three fingers up), big grin. 2) WORKING: holding a clipboard against his chest and writing on it with a pencil, focused smile, eyes looking down at the clipboard. 3) INSPECTING: holding a magnifying glass up to one eye (the eye looks big through the lens), other fist on hip, curious expression. 4) STUCK: one arm raised high with an open palm as if calling for help, worried face, mouth open in a small o, a single sweat drop near his head, a bold black exclamation mark floating above. 5) KNOCKED OUT: lying flat on his back on the floor, arms and legs splayed, X-shaped eyes, wavy mouth, three small cartoon stars circling above his head. 6) ASLEEP: standing slumped with his head tilted, eyes closed, peaceful little smile, arms hanging, three letter Z shapes floating up from his head.
